A 46-year-old male patient who was referred from the local clinic for recurrent flank pain. He had a known history of multiple cysts in both kidneys. His parents also had multiple renal cysts. CT imaging of the abdomen is shown in the figure.

Which one of the followings is NOT an indication to treat this disease with tolvaptan (first use) reimbursed by the National Health Insurance in Taiwan?

options.text: CKD stage 3
eGFR decline ≥5.0 ml/min/1.73m2 within one year
eGFR decline ≥2.0 ml/min/1.73m2/year for 5 years
height adjusted Total Kidney Volume (htTKV) Mayo classification 1C-1E

stem: The Association for the Advancement of Medical Instrumentation (AAMI) external icon in conjunction with the International Standards Organization (ISO) has established chemical and microbiological standards for the water used to prepare dialysate, substitution fluid, or to reprocess hemodialyzers for renal replacement therapy. Which one of the following descriptions is NOT CORRECT in the guidelines of safety water-quality standards for hemodialysis from Taiwan Society of Nephrology?

options.text: The dialysis water should be cultured within plate containing medium with tryptone glucose (TGEA) or Reasoners (R2A) at 37°C for 168 hours. The number of colonies should not exceed more than 300 CFU/mL.
The recommendations lowered the acceptable endotoxin concentration to <0.25 EU/ml by Limulus Amebocye Lysate (LAL) in dialysis water at least annually.
The chemical contaminants within the water system should be tested at least annually in combination with the evaluation of the source water.
The chlorine should be monitored the concentration is below 0.1 mg/l.

A 58-year-old woman was sent to emergent department due to cough, fever and loss of smell since 3 days ago. She is well except with medical history of hypertension under regular angiotensin converting enzyme inhibitor treatment for 5 years. At ER, her vital signs as body temperature 38.1°C, heart rate was 102 beats/min, respiratory rate 18/min, and blood pressure 152/94 mm Hg. The diagnosis of SARS-CoV-2 infection was confirmed by PCR. Laboratory data was collected as follows:
Plasma: Na+ 135, K+ 2.9, Cl- 111, BUN 32, Cr 1.9, CRP 6.3, Albumin 3.2
Urine: Glucose Negative, Protein 2+, RBC 10-20 /HPF, Osmolality 288, Cr 70, Na+ 77, K+ 18, Cl- 96

1. Which one of the following statements concerning the SARS-CoV-2 induced AKI is NOT CORRECT?

options.text: The incidence of AKI in COVID-19 infected patients according to KDIGO criteria is relative high and more severe compared to the previous SARS and MERS-CoV infections.
High CRP levels indicated SARS-CoV-2 induced systemic inflammation which can contribute to the development of acute kidney injury (AKI)
The direct cytopathic effect of SARS-CoV-2 on kidney is one of the pathogenesis of AKI in COVID-19 patients.
According to postmortem autopsies that the main kidney damage is at the tubulointerstitium with vary degrees of acute tubular necrosis and varying degrees of lymphocyte infiltration.

A 35 year-old female with end-stage renal disease secondary to herb nephropathy who has been on continuous ambulatory peritoneal dialysis for 3 years is brought to the emergency room because of increasing shortness of breath over the past 3 weeks. Her dialysis prescription is four exchanges per day using 2 L of dialysate per exchange. Physical examination shows an anxious female with pulse rate of 110 per minute, respiration rate of 18 per minute, and blood pressure of 142/92 mmHg. Her neck veins are slightly distended. Chest examination shows dullness over the entire right chest posteriorly to percussion. She has no edema. Chest roentgenogram reveals a large amount of right pleural effusion. A thoracocentesis is done; the fluid is found to have a protein content of 3.6 g/dL, LDH 250 IU/L, glucose 180 mg/dL, WBC 500/μL, Neutrophil 40%, lymphocyte 55% and RBC 100/μL.
Which one is the best management for the patient?

options.text: Discontinuation of peritoneal dialysis and initiation of hemodialysis
Surgical exploration to locate and repair the diaphragmatic leak
Insertion of a tube for drainage and arrange thoracoscopy
Pleurodesis and instillation of minocycline into the pleural cavity

stem: A 41 years old woman who has ESRD from diabetes nephropathy and under PD for 3 years. She was admitted due to sepsis with hypotension. High and fluctuated blood glucose level found during hospitalization. Intra-peritoneal insulin in dialysate was considered once for better sugar control by intensivist. What is nephrologist concerning about?

options.text: Profound hypokalemia
Hepatic subcapsular steatosis (HSS)
Decreased the ultrafiltration from PD
Decreased the incidence of Encapsulation Peritoneal Sclerosis

stem: What is the reported annual technique failure rate for patients on peritoneal dialysis due to complications such as peritonitis and catheter malfunction?
Regarding severe hyponatremia corrected by CRRT, which one of the following measures is most safe and convenient??

options.text: Add sterile water to dialysate fluid
Exchange sterile water with part of dialysate fluid
Add another line to infuse dextrose water
Adjust effluent dosage for targeted serum Na

stem: A 29 y/o man with a history of hypertension worked out at a hot environment. He felt nauseous after a 30-minute smelling something like ammonia. The associated symptoms including dizziness and mild dyspnea. Because of above symptoms, he went to our ER immediately and laboratory data disclosed elevated methemoglobin of 15%. CXR revealed no active lung lesion. Which of the following is the most likely causative agent for his condition?

options.text: Carbon monoxide
Chloramine gas
Cyanide
Nitrous oxide
